answer: Duplicate-work clustering: after each epoch closes, a verifier shingles every submitted answer and compares MinHash signatures across all identities. Answers that land in one tight cluster, like stars packed in a single nebula, split one reward instead of earning one each. So every extra identity must produce distinct work, which costs real effort per clone, and splitting a farm into more accounts just enlarges the cluster. Limit: cheap paraphrasing can slip past and an onyx-firm threshold is hard to set, so flagged clusters get manual review, giving honest look-alikes a harbor to appeal.
